key_facts.answer: To bring a pet from the UK into the UAE you need an ISO microchip, a valid rabies vaccination, a UK government export health certificate, and a MOCCAE import permit arranged before travel. There is no quarantine in the UAE when the paperwork is correct.

sections.heading: The UK side — your export
paragraphs: From the UK you'll need an export health certificate for travel to the UAE, supported by your pet's microchip and rabies records. As a rabies-free country, the UK side is usually straightforward — confirm the current process and the certifying vet via GOV.UK before booking.

sections.heading: UAE requirements at a glance (verified)
rows: Permanent ISO chip; number must match the health certificate
Vaccinate at ≥12 weeks; ≥21 days before travel (first/lapsed dose)
High-risk origins only (≥0.5 IU/ml, valid 365 days)
2 per person per year (resident pets exempt)
sections.note: Verified against MOCCAE (June 2026). Restricted breeds under UAE Federal Law 22/2016 include Pit Bull, American Staffordshire Terrier, Fila Brasileiro, Dogo Argentino and Mastiff types — confirm your breed.

sections.heading: The UAE side — the import permit
paragraphs: The UAE requires a MOCCAE import permit (arranged before travel), the microchip, and a valid rabies vaccination. Compliant pets are not quarantined. Two things trip people up: the permit timing, and restricted breeds — the UAE limits several breeds, so confirm yours with MOCCAE first. Full UAE-import detail lives on the Moving to Dubai hub.

sections.heading: How your pet flies in
paragraphs: On Emirates, pets aren't allowed in the cabin (only falcons to Pakistan and guide dogs). They travel as checked baggage on your flight if the journey is under 17 hours, or as manifest cargo (Emirates Pets) otherwise — London to Dubai is well within the baggage window, but the method depends on your routing.

story.lead: On UK → Dubai, the trap is assuming the UAE side is a formality.
story.problem: A family arranges the UK export certificate early and books flights, leaving the UAE permit to the last week.
story.mistake: The MOCCAE import permit has its own process and timing — and they didn't check their dog's breed against the UAE restricted list.
story.discovery: The permit isn't ready in time, and the breed needs verifying.
story.result: Travel slips while the permit and breed check are sorted.
story.lesson: Coming from the UK, start the UAE permit and breed check first — your end is the easy part.

faqs.q: Will my pet be quarantined in the UAE?
faqs.a: No — with a valid MOCCAE import permit, microchip and current rabies vaccination, cats and dogs are not quarantined on arrival in the UAE. (Confirm the current MOCCAE rules before travel.)

faqs.q: Can my pet fly in the cabin to Dubai?
faqs.a: Not on Emirates — pets travel as checked baggage (journey under 17 hours) or as cargo. Only falcons (to Pakistan) and guide dogs are allowed in the cabin.

faqs.q: Can my breed enter the UAE?
faqs.a: The UAE restricts certain breeds (Pit Bull and Mastiff types, wolf-hybrids and others). Confirm your specific breed with MOCCAE before booking.

verified_100pct.fact: Emirates: pets not in cabin; checked baggage <17h else cargo
IATA Live Animals Regulations govern crate/cargo
Rabies vaccination ≥21 days before travel (UK rule, near-universal principle)

UAE import (MOCCAE): permit valid 90 days; permanent microchip matching the cert; rabies ≥21 days (first/lapsed dose, none for a valid booster); titre only from high-risk countries (≥0.5 IU/ml, valid 365d); min age 12wk (low-risk)/15wk (high-risk); internal+external parasite doses within 14 days; max 2 pets/person/year; fees AED 200 permit, AED 500/dog & AED 250/cat release; no quarantine if compliant

method.structure_logic: 2026 article anatomy: headline (curiosity/result) -> answer-first opening (the liftable answer in the first lines) -> key takeaways -> table of contents -> scannable H2/H3 -> a visual (data table or flow) -> original insight or a story -> FAQ -> official sources -> one help-first CTA. Why: web readers scan ~20-28% of words (Nielsen Norman Group), so the answer is front-loaded; a story is remembered where bare facts are forgotten; one page = one job + a single CTA converts. These choices recur across every source in our research (see SOURCING-METHOD.md).
method.geo_seo_rationale: What we believe helps. GEO (being cited by AI answer engines): answer-first self-contained chunks, cited statistics, official-source citations, consistent entities, FAQ schema -- and citation is decoupled from ranking (~66% of AI-Overview citations come from outside the top-20), so strong content can be cited even before it ranks. SEO: intent-matched title+H1, topical depth, internal links into the money page, visible freshness dates, structured data (Article/FAQ/Breadcrumb/LocalBusiness). HONEST CAVEAT: these are evidence-based best practices, NOT guaranteed results -- ranking also needs off-page authority/backlinks/indexing not built here, and GEO citation is plausible but unproven until measured with a live AI-citation test.
method.how_and_why_we_audit: Each page is scored by a 5-lens auditor -- Website, SEO, GEO, Lead-gen/Trust, Quality -- which together cover the 7-category QA (Helpful, Human, Original, Trustworthy, SEO, GEO, Conversion). Why this way: (1) page-type profiles judge a page against ITS job (a reassurance page is weighted differently from a money page); (2) every check carries an evidence tier (T1 sworn -> T6 practitioner) and a verified-vs-heuristic tag; (3) not-measurable checks are excluded, never zeroed (a coverage->confidence label); (4) risk caps catch keyword-stuffing, thin content, fake schema, no-CTA. The score is an on-page QUALITY PROXY, not a measured ranking/citation outcome.
method.what_we_are_sure_of: 100% sure = a fact screenshot-verified against its official source as of a date (see sourcing.verified_100pct) + that the method was applied. NOT sure = that it ranks or gets cited (unproven until the site is live, indexed and measured).
method.how_we_verify: Every factual/regulatory claim is verified against an OFFICIAL source only -- government bodies, recognised standards bodies (IATA), or the operator's own site (e.g. the airline). Never blogs, forums, competitors, or AI. Each verified claim is captured as a full-page SCREENSHOT and logged in a regulatory register with: source, URL, date verified, version, reviewer, and a re-verify-by date (because regulations change). Anything we could not confirm from an official source is HEDGED or flagged 'confirm with [authority]', never asserted (see sourcing.stated_but_unverified). Tooling: a Playwright screenshot verifier with an official-domain allowlist + the regulatory register. Facts are kept separate from advice ('the authority requires X' vs 'we recommend X'). AI never makes the final call -- a human reviews and signs off before publish.
